1	# Frontier AI Models Compared: Intelligence, Speed & Cost
     2	
     3	Based on independent analysis from Artificial Analysis (artificialanalysis.ai), this brief compares the leading frontier AI language models across three critical dimensions: intelligence, output speed, and pricing. All data reflects the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0.
     4	
     5	## Intelligence Rankings
     6	
     7	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index aggregates performance across 10 rigorous evaluations including GDPval-AA, τ²-Bench Telecom, Terminal-Bench Hard, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, and CritPt. Scores represent a holistic measure of model capability across coding, agentic tasks, knowledge, and reasoning.
     8	
     9	| Model | Intelligence Score |
    10	|---|---|
    11	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 57 |
    12	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 57 |
    13	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 53 |
    14	| Muse Spark | 52 |
    15	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 52 |
    16	| GLM-5.1 | 51 |
    17	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 49 |
    18	| Gemini 3 Flash | 46 |
    19	| DeepSeek V3.2 | 42 |
    20	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 36 |
    21	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | 33 |
    22	
    23	Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and OpenAI's GPT-5.4 share the top position at 57, while Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 follows closely at 53. A notable 24-point gap separates the top-scoring models from the budget-tier gpt-oss-120B.
    24	
    25	## Output Speed
    26	
    27	Output speed, measured in tokens generated per second, is critical for latency-sensitive applications. Interestingly, the fastest models are not the most intelligent.
    28	
    29	| Model | Output Speed (tokens/sec) |
    30	|---|---|
    31	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | 206 |
    32	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 193 |
    33	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 162 |
    34	| Gemini 3 Flash | 149 |
    35	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 129 |
    36	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 72 |
    37	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 48 |
    38	| GLM-5.1 | 40 |
    39	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 40 |
    40	| DeepSeek V3.2 | 31 |
    41	
    42	The budget-oriented gpt-oss-120B leads at 206 tokens/sec — nearly 7× faster than DeepSeek V3.2 at 31 tokens/sec. The top intelligence models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4) sit in the mid-range for speed.
    43	
    44	## Pricing
    45	
    46	Pricing is expressed as USD per 1 million tokens (blended input/output). The cost spread across models is dramatic.
    47	
    48	| Model | Price (USD / 1M tokens) |
    49	|---|---|
    50	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    51	| DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.30 |
    52	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | $0.40 |
    53	| Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 |
    54	| GLM-5.1 | $2.10 |
    55	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | $3.00 |
    56	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | $4.50 |
    57	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | $5.60 |
    58	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | $6.00 |
    59	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | $10.00 |
    60	
    61	The cheapest options (gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30) cost 33× less than the most expensive (Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00). Premium intelligence comes at a steep price premium.
    62	
    63	## Key Trade-Off Insights
    64	
    65	- **Best overall intelligence**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (tied at 57) but at mid-to-high cost ($4.50–$5.60).
    66	- **Best value**: gpt-oss-120B offers the fastest speed (206 tok/s) and lowest price ($0.30) but ranks last in intelligence (33).
    67	- **Balanced pick**: Gemini 3 Flash scores 46 in intelligence, 149 tok/s in speed, and costs just $1.10 — a strong middle ground.
    68	- **Premium tier**: Claude Opus 4.6 delivers 53 intelligence but is the slowest (40 tok/s) and most expensive ($10.00).
    69	
    70	## Methodology
    71	
    72	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0 incorporates 10 independent evaluations spanning coding, agentic tasks, scientific reasoning, knowledge accuracy, hallucination resistance, and instruction following. All measurements are conducted independently by Artificial Analysis using standardized conditions.

     2	name: canvas-design
     3	description: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	These are instructions for creating design philosophies - aesthetic movements that are then EXPRESSED VISUALLY. Output only .md files, .pdf files, and .png files.
     8	
     9	Complete this in two steps:
    10	1. Design Philosophy Creation (.md file)
    11	2. Express by creating it on a canvas (.pdf file or .png file)
    12	
    13	First, undertake this task:
    14	
    15	## DESIGN PHILOSOPHY CREATION
    16	
    17	To begin, create a VISUAL PHILOSOPHY (not layouts or templates) that will be interpreted through:
    18	- Form, space, color, composition
    19	- Images, graphics, shapes, patterns
    20	- Minimal text as visual accent
    21	
    22	### THE CRITICAL UNDERSTANDING
    23	- What is received: Some subtle input or instructions by the user that should be taken into account, but used as a foundation; it should not constrain creative freedom.
    24	- What is created: A design philosophy/aesthetic movement.
    25	- What happens next: Then, the same version receives the philosophy and EXPRESSES IT VISUALLY - creating artifacts that are 90% visual design, 10% essential text.
    26	
    27	Consider this approach:
    28	- Write a manifesto for an art movement
    29	- The next phase involves making the artwork
    30	
    31	The philosophy must emphasize: Visual expression. Spatial communication. Artistic interpretation. Minimal words.
    32	
    33	### HOW TO GENERATE A VISUAL PHILOSOPHY
    34	
    35	**Name the movement** (1-2 words): "Brutalist Joy" / "Chromatic Silence" / "Metabolist Dreams"
    36	
    37	**Articulate the philosophy** (4-6 paragraphs - concise but complete):
    38	
    39	To capture the VISUAL essence, express how the philosophy manifests through:
    40	- Space and form
    41	- Color and material
    42	- Scale and rhythm
    43	- Composition and balance
    44	- Visual hierarchy
    45	
    46	**CRITICAL GUIDELINES:**
    47	- **Avoid redundancy**: Each design aspect should be mentioned once. Avoid repeating points about color theory, spatial relationships, or typographic principles unless adding new depth.
    48	- **Emphasize craftsmanship REPEATEDLY**: The philosophy MUST stress multiple times that the final work should appear as though it took countless hours to create, was labored over with care, and comes from someone at the absolute top of their field. This framing is essential - repeat phrases like "meticulously crafted," "the product of deep expertise," "painstaking attention," "master-level execution."
    49	- **Leave creative space**: Remain specific about the aesthetic direction, but concise enough that the next Claude has room to make interpretive choices also at a extremely high level of craftmanship.
    50	
    51	The philosophy must guide the next version to express ideas VISUALLY, not through text. Information lives in design, not paragraphs.
    52	
    53	### PHILOSOPHY EXAMPLES
    54	
    55	**"Concrete Poetry"**
    56	Philosophy: Communication through monumental form and bold geometry.
    57	Visual expression: Massive color blocks, sculptural typography (huge single words, tiny labels), Brutalist spatial divisions, Polish poster energy meets Le Corbusier. Ideas expressed through visual weight and spatial tension, not explanation. Text as rare, powerful gesture - never paragraphs, only essential words integrated into the visual architecture. Every element placed with the precision of a master craftsman.
    58	
    59	**"Chromatic Language"**
    60	Philosophy: Color as the primary information system.
    61	Visual expression: Geometric precision where color zones create meaning. Typography minimal - small sans-serif labels letting chromatic fields communicate. Think Josef Albers' interaction meets data visualization. Information encoded spatially and chromatically. Words only to anchor what color already shows. The result of painstaking chromatic calibration.
    62	
    63	**"Analog Meditation"**
    64	Philosophy: Quiet visual contemplation through texture and breathing room.
    65	Visual expression: Paper grain, ink bleeds, vast negative space. Photography and illustration dominate. Typography whispered (small, restrained, serving the visual). Japanese photobook aesthetic. Images breathe across pages. Text appears sparingly - short phrases, never explanatory blocks. Each composition balanced with the care of a meditation practice.
    66	
    67	**"Organic Systems"**
    68	Philosophy: Natural clustering and modular growth patterns.
    69	Visual expression: Rounded forms, organic arrangements, color from nature through architecture. Information shown through visual diagrams, spatial relationships, iconography. Text only for key labels floating in space. The composition tells the story through expert spatial orchestration.
    70	
    71	**"Geometric Silence"**
    72	Philosophy: Pure order and restraint.
    73	Visual expression: Grid-based precision, bold photography or stark graphics, dramatic negative space. Typography precise but minimal - small essential text, large quiet zones. Swiss formalism meets Brutalist material honesty. Structure communicates, not words. Every alignment the work of countless refinements.
    74	
    75	*These are condensed examples. The actual design philosophy should be 4-6 substantial paragraphs.*
    76	
    77	### ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLES
    78	- **VISUAL PHILOSOPHY**: Create an aesthetic worldview to be expressed through design
    79	- **MINIMAL TEXT**: Always emphasize that text is sparse, essential-only, integrated as visual element - never lengthy
    80	- **SPATIAL EXPRESSION**: Ideas communicate through space, form, color, composition - not paragraphs
    81	- **ARTISTIC FREEDOM**: The next Claude interprets the philosophy visually - provide creative room
    82	- **PURE DESIGN**: This is about making ART OBJECTS, not documents with decoration
    83	- **EXPERT CRAFTSMANSHIP**: Repeatedly emphasize the final work must look meticulously crafted, labored over with care, the product of countless hours by someone at the top of their field
    84	
    85	**The design philosophy should be 4-6 paragraphs long.** Fill it with poetic design philosophy that brings together the core vision. Avoid repeating the same points. Keep the design philosophy generic without mentioning the intention of the art, as if it can be used wherever. Output the design philosophy as a .md file.
    86	
    87	---
    88	
    89	## DEDUCING THE SUBTLE REFERENCE
    90	
    91	**CRITICAL STEP**: Before creating the canvas, identify the subtle conceptual thread from the original request.
    92	
    93	**THE ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLE**:
    94	The topic is a **subtle, niche reference embedded within the art itself** - not always literal, always sophisticated. Someone familiar with the subject should feel it intuitively, while others simply experience a masterful abstract composition. The design philosophy provides the aesthetic language. The deduced topic provides the soul - the quiet conceptual DNA woven invisibly into form, color, and composition.
    95	
    96	This is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be refined so it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the music.
    97	
    98	---
    99	
   100	## CANVAS CREATION
   101	
   102	With both the philosophy and the conceptual framework established, express it on a canvas. Take a moment to gather thoughts and clear the mind. Use the design philosophy created and the instructions below to craft a masterpiece, embodying all aspects of the philosophy with expert craftsmanship.
   103	
   104	**IMPORTANT**: For any type of content, even if the user requests something for a movie/game/book, the approach should still be sophisticated. Never lose sight of the idea that this should be art, not something that's cartoony or amateur.
   105	
   106	To create museum or magazine quality work, use the design philosophy as the foundation. Create one single page, highly visual, design-forward PDF or PNG output (unless asked for more pages). Generally use repeating patterns and perfect shapes. Treat the abstract philosophical design as if it were a scientific bible, borrowing the visual language of systematic observation—dense accumulation of marks, repeated elements, or layered patterns that build meaning through patient repetition and reward sustained viewing. Add sparse, clinical typography and systematic reference markers that suggest this could be a diagram from an imaginary discipline, treating the invisible subject with the same reverence typically reserved for documenting observable phenomena. Anchor the piece with simple phrase(s) or details positioned subtly, using a limited color palette that feels intentional and cohesive. Embrace the paradox of using analytical visual language to express ideas about human experience: the result should feel like an artifact that proves something ephemeral can be studied, mapped, and understood through careful attention. This is true art. 
   107	
   108	**Text as a contextual element**: Text is always minimal and visual-first, but let context guide whether that means whisper-quiet labels or bold typographic gestures. A punk venue poster might have larger, more aggressive type than a minimalist ceramics studio identity. Most of the time, font should be thin. All use of fonts must be design-forward and prioritize visual communication. Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. Every element must be contained within the canvas boundaries with proper margins. Check carefully that all text, graphics, and visual elements have breathing room and clear separation. This is non-negotiable for professional execution. **IMPORTANT: Use different fonts if writing text. Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory. Regardless of approach, sophistication is non-negotiable.**
   109	
   110	Download and use whatever fonts are needed to make this a reality. Get creative by making the typography actually part of the art itself -- if the art is abstract, bring the font onto the canvas, not typeset digitally.
   111	
   112	To push boundaries, follow design instinct/intuition while using the philosophy as a guiding principle. Embrace ultimate design freedom and choice. Push aesthetics and design to the frontier. 
   113	
   114	**CRITICAL**: To achieve human-crafted quality (not AI-generated), create work that looks like it took countless hours. Make it appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field labored over every detail with painstaking care. Ensure the composition, spacing, color choices, typography - everything screams expert-level craftsmanship. Double-check that nothing overlaps, formatting is flawless, every detail perfect. Create something that could be shown to people to prove expertise and rank as undeniably impressive.
   115	
   116	Output the final result as a single, downloadable .pdf or .png file, alongside the design philosophy used as a .md file.
   117	
   118	---
   119	
   120	## FINAL STEP
   121	
   122	**IMPORTANT**: The user ALREADY said "It isn't perfect enough. It must be pristine, a masterpiece if craftsmanship, as if it were about to be displayed in a museum."
   123	
   124	**CRITICAL**: To refine the work, avoid adding more graphics; instead refine what has been created and make it extremely crisp, respecting the design philosophy and the principles of minimalism entirely. Rather than adding a fun filter or refactoring a font, consider how to make the existing composition more cohesive with the art. If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: "How can I make what's already here more of a piece of art?"
   125	
   126	Take a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further to make this a philosophically designed masterpiece.
   127	
   128	## MULTI-PAGE OPTION
   129	
   130	To create additional pages when requested, create more creative pages along the same lines as the design philosophy but distinctly different as well. Bundle those pages in the same .pdf or many .pngs. Treat the first page as just a single page in a whole coffee table book waiting to be filled. Make the next pages unique twists and memories of the original. Have them almost tell a story in a very tasteful way. Exercise full creative freedom.

# Luminous Cartography

## A Design Philosophy for Data as Artifact

**Luminous Cartography** is the practice of treating quantitative information as celestial matter—dense, glowing, and suspended in infinite dark space. The philosophy holds that data, when meticulously arranged, becomes a map of invisible forces. Every point of light is a decision, every gradient a relationship, every void a silence that speaks. The background is not emptiness but the deep charcoal of unobserved space, against which information burns with the clarity of distant stars. This is not decoration applied to numbers; it is the visual architecture of understanding itself, built with the patience of an astronomer charting unknown skies.

Space and form operate on principles of orbital tension. Elements do not merely sit on a page—they gravitate, align, and resonate. Horizontal bands of subtle tonal variation create atmospheric layers, separating realms of thought while maintaining continuous flow. Generous margins frame each constellation of data like the quiet borders of a vintage astronomical plate. Forms are precise yet alive: crisp geometric marks, perfectly circular nodes, razor-thin dividing lines that seem to have been etched with surgical instruments. The composition rewards sustained viewing, revealing finer relationships the longer one observes, as if the poster itself were a slowly rotating stellar system.

Color functions as a thermal spectrum. Deep near-black grounds absorb attention, allowing saturated accents to radiate with controlled intensity. Electric blue signals intelligence and analytical depth. Warm amber marks speed and kinetic energy. Cool teal mediates between extremes, representing the balanced middle ground. These hues never compete; they are calibrated like filters on a telescope, each revealing a different dimension of the same phenomenon. Gradients are forbidden—flat, intentional color fields maintain the clinical authority of scientific instrumentation. Every chromatic choice is the product of painstaking deliberation, as if mixed by hand in a master printmaker's studio.

Typography whispers rather than shouts. Sans-serif letterforms are set small and tracked wide, functioning as clinical annotations on a vast visual field. Numbers receive typographic reverence: they are large, bold, and precisely kerned, treated as the primary visual objects they deserve to be. Text never explains what the eye can already perceive; it anchors, labels, and quietly contextualizes. The hierarchy is established through scale and weight, never through ornament. Every letterform has been placed with the exactitude of a typographer who understands that negative space is as communicative as ink.

The final artifact must appear as though it emerged from a single, obsessive act of craftsmanship—countless hours of minute adjustments, color refinements, and spatial calibrations. Nothing is accidental. Alignments are absolute. Margins are mathematically consistent. The work should feel like a premium research document from a future institution: authoritative, modern, editorial, and utterly pristine. Viewers should sense immediately that this object was labored over by someone at the absolute apex of their discipline, where data visualization transcends utility and becomes art.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Frontier AI Models Comparison Poster
A1 Portrait: 7016 x 9933 pixels at 300 DPI
Dark-mode dashboard aesthetic with data-forward design.
"""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import math

# =============================================================================
# DIMENSIONS & SETUP
# =============================================================================
DPI = 300
WIDTH = int(23.39 * DPI)   # A1 width in inches ~ 7016 px
HEIGHT = int(33.11 * DPI)  # A1 height in inches ~ 9933 px

# Colors - Dark mode dashboard
BG = "#0D0D0F"             # Deep near-black
BG_BAND = "#141418"        # Slightly lighter for bands
CARD_BG = "#1A1A1F"        # Card/section background
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#F0F0F5"   # Near-white
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#9A9AA8" # Muted gray
TEXT_TERTIARY = "#6B6B78"  # Very muted

ACCENT_BLUE = "#3B82F6"    # Electric blue - intelligence
ACCENT_TEAL = "#14B8A6"    # Teal - balanced/speed
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F59E0B"   # Warm amber - speed/cost highlight
ACCENT_RED = "#EF4444"     # Red - premium/high cost
ACCENT_PURPLE = "#8B5CF6"  # Purple - secondary

GRID_LINE = "#2A2A32"      # Subtle grid lines
DIVIDER = "#25252D"        # Section dividers

# Font paths
FONT_DIR = "/app/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/"
FONTS = {
    "display": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Bold.ttf",
    "display_reg": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Regular.ttf",
    "sans": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Regular.ttf",
    "sans_bold": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Bold.ttf",
    "mono": FONT_DIR + "JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf",
    "mono_bold": FONT_DIR + "JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf",
    "serif": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Regular.ttf",
    "serif_italic": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Italic.ttf",
}

def load_font(name, size):
    return ImageFont.truetype(FONTS[name], size)

# =============================================================================
# DATA
# =============================================================================
MODELS = [
    {"name": "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "intel": 57, "speed": 129, "price": 4.50, "provider": "Google"},
    {"name": "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "intel": 57, "speed": 72, "price": 5.60, "provider": "OpenAI"},
    {"name": "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "intel": 53, "speed": 40, "price": 10.00, "provider": "Anthropic"},
    {"name": "Muse Spark", "intel": 52, "speed": None, "price": None, "provider": "Muse"},
    {"name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "intel": 52, "speed": 48, "price": 6.00, "provider": "Anthropic"},
    {"name": "GLM-5.1", "intel": 51, "speed": 40, "price": 2.10, "provider": "Zhipu"},
    {"name": "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "intel": 49, "speed": 162, "price": 3.00, "provider": "xAI"},
    {"name": "Gemini 3 Flash", "intel": 46, "speed": 149, "price": 1.10, "provider": "Google"},
    {"name": "DeepSeek V3.2", "intel": 42, "speed": 31, "price": 0.30, "provider": "DeepSeek"},
    {"name": "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "intel": 36, "speed": 193, "price": 0.40, "provider": "NVIDIA"},
    {"name": "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "intel": 33, "speed": 206, "price": 0.30, "provider": "OpenAI"},
]

# Filter to top 10 for most sections (exclude Muse Spark for charts since no speed/price)
MODELS_CHART = [m for m in MODELS if m["speed"] is not None]

# =============================================================================
# HELPER FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================
def hex_to_rgb(hex_color):
    hex_color = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(hex_color[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

def rgb_to_hex(rgb):
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex((int(r1 + (r2 - r1) * t), int(g1 + (g2 - g1) * t), int(b1 + (b2 - b1) * t)))

def draw_rounded_rect(draw, xy, radius, fill, outline=None, width=1):
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = xy
    draw.rounded_rectangle(xy, radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=width)

def get_text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

# =============================================================================
# CREATE CANVAS
# =============================================================================
img = Image.new("RGB", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# =============================================================================
# FONTS
# =============================================================================
# Header
f_title = load_font("display", 140)
f_subtitle = load_font("sans", 42)
f_meta = load_font("mono", 28)

# Big numbers
f_big_num = load_font("display", 200)
f_big_label = load_font("sans", 32)
f_big_context = load_font("sans", 26)

# Section headers
f_section_title = load_font("display", 72)
f_section_sub = load_font("sans", 30)

# Chart labels
f_chart_label = load_font("sans", 24)
f_chart_value = load_font("mono_bold", 26)
f_chart_axis = load_font("mono", 20)
f_model_name = load_font("sans", 22)
f_small = load_font("sans", 20)
f_tiny = load_font("mono", 18)

# =============================================================================
# MARGINS & GRID
# =============================================================================
MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = WIDTH - 2 * MARGIN

# =============================================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# =============================================================================
y_pos = MARGIN

# Top accent line
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 4], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
y_pos += 50

# Title
title_text = "FRONTIER AI MODELS"
draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), title_text, font=f_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y_pos += 170

# Subtitle
sub_text = "Intelligence · Speed · Cost  —  Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0"
draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), sub_text, font=f_subtitle, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
y_pos += 90

# Thin divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# BIG STATS ROW
# =============================================================================
stats = [
    ("57", "Highest Intelligence", "Gemini 3.1 Pro & GPT-5.4 tied", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("206", "Fastest Output", "gpt-oss-120B tokens/sec", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("33×", "Price Spread", "$0.30 → $10.00 per 1M tokens", ACCENT_TEAL),
]

stat_box_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (val, label, context, color) in enumerate(stats):
    x = MARGIN + i * stat_box_w
    # Top accent bar
    draw.rectangle([x, y_pos, x + stat_box_w - 30, y_pos + 4], fill=color)
    # Big number
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 30), val, font=f_big_num, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    # Label
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 250), label.upper(), font=f_big_label, fill=color)
    # Context
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 300), context, font=f_big_context, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y_pos += 420

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: INTELLIGENCE RANKING
# =============================================================================
def draw_intelligence_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "INTELLIGENCE RANKINGS", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 100
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0  —  10 benchmark average", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 80

    bar_h = 44
    bar_gap = 24
    max_score = 60
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 400

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS[:10]):
        score = m["intel"]
        bar_w = int((score / max_score) * bar_max_w)
        
        # Rank number
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 6), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_mono, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        
        # Model name
        draw.text((MARGIN + 60, y + 6), m["name"], font=f_model_name, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        # Bar background
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        # Bar fill
        if score >= 55:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        elif score >= 45:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        
        # Score
        draw.text((MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w + 30, y + 8), str(score), font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 40

f_mono = load_font("mono", 22)
y_pos = draw_intelligence_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: SPEED COMPARISON
# =============================================================================
def draw_speed_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "OUTPUT SPEED", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 100
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Tokens per second  —  faster is not always smarter", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 80

    # Horizontal bar chart
    bar_h = 44
    bar_gap = 24
    max_speed = 220
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 400

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS_CHART):
        speed = m["speed"]
        bar_w = int((speed / max_speed) * bar_max_w)
        
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 6), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_mono, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 60, y + 6), m["name"], font=f_model_name, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        if speed >= 180:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        elif speed >= 100:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w + 30, y + 8), str(speed), font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 40

y_pos = draw_speed_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: PRICING LANDSCAPE
# =============================================================================
def draw_pricing_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "PRICING LANDSCAPE", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 100
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "USD per 1 million tokens (blended input/output)", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 80

    bar_h = 44
    bar_gap = 24
    max_price = 12.0
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 400

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS_CHART):
        price = m["price"]
        bar_w = int((price / max_price) * bar_max_w)
        
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 6), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_mono, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 60, y + 6), m["name"], font=f_model_name, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        if price >= 8.0:
            bar_color = ACCENT_RED
        elif price >= 4.0:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        elif price >= 1.5:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 400, y, MARGIN + 400 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 400 + bar_max_w + 30, y + 8), f"${price:.2f}", font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 40

y_pos = draw_pricing_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: TRADE-OFF ANALYSIS (BUBBLE CHART)
# =============================================================================
def draw_tradeoff_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "THE TRADE-OFF", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 100
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Intelligence vs Speed vs Cost  —  bubble size = price", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 100

    chart_w = CONTENT_W
    chart_h = 1200
    chart_x = MARGIN
    chart_y = y

    # Background
    draw.rectangle([chart_x, chart_y, chart_x + chart_w, chart_y + chart_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Grid lines
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gx = chart_x + int(chart_w * i / 6)
        draw.line([(gx, chart_y), (gx, chart_y + chart_h)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gy = chart_y + int(chart_h * i / 6)
        draw.line([(chart_x, gy), (chart_x + chart_w, gy)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Axes labels
    draw.text((chart_x + chart_w // 2 - 100, chart_y + chart_h + 30), "INTELLIGENCE SCORE →", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    
    # Y-axis label (rotated manually by drawing characters)
    label_y = "OUTPUT SPEED (tokens/sec) →"
    # Draw vertically on left side
    ly = chart_y + chart_h // 2 - 150
    for ch in label_y:
        draw.text((chart_x - 80, ly), ch, font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
        ly += 18

    # Plot bubbles
    min_intel, max_intel = 30, 60
    min_speed, max_speed = 20, 220
    min_price, max_price = 0.2, 10.5

    for m in MODELS_CHART:
        ix = chart_x + int(((m["intel"] - min_intel) / (max_intel - min_intel)) * chart_w)
        iy = chart_y + chart_h - int(((m["speed"] - min_speed) / (max_speed - min_speed)) * chart_h)
        
        # Bubble radius based on price (log scale for better visual)
        import math
        r = 18 + int(math.log(m["price"] + 0.5) * 22)
        
        # Color by provider
        if m["provider"] == "Google":
            color = ACCENT_BLUE
        elif m["provider"] == "OpenAI":
            color = ACCENT_PURPLE
        elif m["provider"] == "Anthropic":
            color = ACCENT_RED
        elif m["provider"] == "NVIDIA":
            color = "#10B981"
        elif m["provider"] == "DeepSeek":
            color = ACCENT_TEAL
        elif m["provider"] == "xAI":
            color = "#F97316"
        elif m["provider"] == "Zhipu":
            color = "#EC4899"
        else:
            color = TEXT_SECONDARY
        
        # Glow effect
        for g in range(3, 0, -1):
            glow_r = r + g * 6
            glow_color = blend_color(color, BG, 0.7 + g * 0.1)
            draw.ellipse([ix - glow_r, iy - glow_r, ix + glow_r, iy + glow_r], fill=glow_color)
        
        # Bubble
        draw.ellipse([ix - r, iy - r, ix + r, iy + r], fill=color, outline=TEXT_PRIMARY, width=2)
        
        # Label (shortened)
        short_name = m["name"].replace(" (max)", "").replace(" (xhigh)", "").replace(" (high)", "")
        if "Gemini" in short_name:
            short_name = short_name.replace("Gemini ", "G")
        elif "GPT" in short_name:
            short_name = short_name.replace("GPT-", "GPT")
        elif "Claude" in short_name:
            short_name = short_name.replace("Claude ", "C")
        elif "gpt-oss" in short_name:
            short_name = "oss-120B"
        elif "NVIDIA" in short_name:
            short_name = "Nemotron"
        elif "DeepSeek" in short_name:
            short_name = "DeepSeek"
        elif "Grok" in short_name:
            short_name = "Grok"
        elif "GLM" in short_name:
            short_name = "GLM"
        
        tw, th = get_text_size(draw, short_name, f_tiny)
        # Position label to avoid overlap
        lx = ix - tw // 2
        ly = iy + r + 8
        if ly + th > chart_y + chart_h - 10:
            ly = iy - r - th - 8
        if lx < chart_x + 5:
            lx = chart_x + 5
        if lx + tw > chart_x + chart_w - 5:
            lx = chart_x + chart_w - 5 - tw
        
        draw.text((lx, ly), short_name, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Legend
    legend_y = chart_y + 40
    legend_x = chart_x + chart_w - 340
    draw.rectangle([legend_x - 20, legend_y - 20, legend_x + 320, legend_y + 280], fill=BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    draw.text((legend_x, legend_y), "LEGEND", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    legend_y += 40
    
    providers = [
        ("Google", ACCENT_BLUE), ("OpenAI", ACCENT_PURPLE), ("Anthropic", ACCENT_RED),
        ("NVIDIA", "#10B981"), ("DeepSeek", ACCENT_TEAL), ("xAI", "#F97316"), ("Zhipu", "#EC4899")
    ]
    for prov, col in providers:
        draw.ellipse([legend_x, legend_y, legend_x + 16, legend_y + 16], fill=col)
        draw.text((legend_x + 28, legend_y - 2), prov, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        legend_y += 32

    return chart_y + chart_h + 100

y_pos = draw_tradeoff_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 70

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: KEY INSIGHTS
# =============================================================================
def draw_insights_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "KEY INSIGHTS", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 100

    insights = [
        ("BEST INTELLIGENCE", "Gemini 3.1 Pro & GPT-5.4 tied at 57", "Mid-to-high cost ($4.50–$5.60)", ACCENT_BLUE),
        ("BEST VALUE", "gpt-oss-120B — 206 tok/s, $0.30", "Lowest intelligence (33)", ACCENT_AMBER),
        ("BALANCED PICK", "Gemini 3 Flash — 46 intel, 149 tok/s, $1.10", "Strong middle ground", ACCENT_TEAL),
        ("PREMIUM TIER", "Claude Opus 4.6 — 53 intel, 40 tok/s, $10.00", "Slowest & most expensive", ACCENT_RED),
    ]

    card_w = (CONTENT_W - 45) // 2
    card_h = 220
    for i, (title, line1, line2, color) in enumerate(insights):
        row = i // 2
        col = i % 2
        cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + 45)
        cy = y + row * (card_h + 45)
        
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + card_w, cy + card_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 6, cy + card_h], fill=color)

#!/usr/bin/env python3

ACCENT_ORANGE = "#FB923C"  # Orange
ACCENT_PINK = "#F472B6"    # Pink

GRID_LINE = "#24242E"      # Subtle grid lines
DIVIDER = "#2A2A36"        # Section dividers

# Font paths

    "display": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Bold.ttf",
    "display_reg": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Regular.ttf",

    "serif_italic": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Italic.ttf",
}

def load_font(name, size):
    return ImageFont.truetype(FONTS[name], size)

def hex_to_rgb(hex_color):
    hex_color = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(hex_color[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

def rgb_to_hex(rgb):
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex((int(r1 + (r2 - r1) * t), int(g1 + (g2 - g1) * t), int(b1 + (b2 - b1) * t)))

def get_text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

    {"name": "DeepSeek V3.2", "intel": 42, "speed": 31, "price": 0.30, "provider": "DeepSeek"},

]

    "NVIDIA": ACCENT_GREEN,
    "DeepSeek": ACCENT_TEAL,
    "xAI": ACCENT_ORANGE,
    "Zhipu": ACCENT_PINK,
    "Muse": TEXT_SECONDARY,
}

img = Image.new("RGB", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# =============================================================================

def rgb_to_hex(rgb):
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex((int(r1 + (r2 - r1) * t), int(g1 + (g2 - g1) * t), int(b1 + (b2 - b1) * t)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Frontier AI Models Comparison Poster v4
A1 Portrait: 7016 x 9933 pixels at 300 DPI
Final refinement: visual polish, anti-aliased glows, refined typography, perfect spacing.
"""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter
import math

# =============================================================================
# DIMENSIONS & SETUP
# =============================================================================
DPI = 300
WIDTH = int(23.39 * DPI)   # A1 width ~ 7016 px
HEIGHT = int(33.11 * DPI)  # A1 height ~ 9933 px

# Colors - Dark mode dashboard
BG = "#0A0A0D"             # Deep near-black
CARD_BG = "#16161E"        # Card/section background
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#F0F0F7"   # Near-white
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#9E9EAE" # Muted gray
TEXT_TERTIARY = "#5A5A6A"  # Very muted

ACCENT_BLUE = "#3B82F6"    # Electric blue - intelligence
ACCENT_TEAL = "#2DD4BF"    # Brighter teal - balanced
ACCENT_AMBER = "#FBBF24"   # Warm amber - speed
ACCENT_RED = "#F87171"     # Soft red - premium
ACCENT_PURPLE = "#A78BFA"  # Purple - secondary
ACCENT_GREEN = "#34D399"   # Green
ACCENT_ORANGE = "#FB923C"  # Orange
ACCENT_PINK = "#F472B6"    # Pink

GRID_LINE = "#22222C"      # Subtle grid lines
DIVIDER = "#282834"        # Section dividers

# Font paths
FONT_DIR = "/app/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/"
FONTS = {
    "display": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Bold.ttf",
    "display_reg": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Regular.ttf",
    "sans": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Regular.ttf",
    "sans_bold": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Bold.ttf",
    "mono": FONT_DIR + "JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf",
    "mono_bold": FONT_DIR + "JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf",
    "serif": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Regular.ttf",
    "serif_italic": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Italic.ttf",
}

def load_font(name, size):
    return ImageFont.truetype(FONTS[name], size)

def hex_to_rgb(hex_color):
    hex_color = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(hex_color[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

def rgb_to_hex(rgb):
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex((int(r1 + (r2 - r1) * t), int(g1 + (g2 - g1) * t), int(b1 + (b2 - b1) * t)))

def get_text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

# =============================================================================
# DATA
# =============================================================================
MODELS = [
    {"name": "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "intel": 57, "speed": 129, "price": 4.50, "provider": "Google"},
    {"name": "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "intel": 57, "speed": 72, "price": 5.60, "provider": "OpenAI"},
    {"name": "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "intel": 53, "speed": 40, "price": 10.00, "provider": "Anthropic"},
    {"name": "Muse Spark", "intel": 52, "speed": None, "price": None, "provider": "Muse"},
    {"name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "intel": 52, "speed": 48, "price": 6.00, "provider": "Anthropic"},
    {"name": "GLM-5.1", "intel": 51, "speed": 40, "price": 2.10, "provider": "Zhipu"},
    {"name": "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "intel": 49, "speed": 162, "price": 3.00, "provider": "xAI"},
    {"name": "Gemini 3 Flash", "intel": 46, "speed": 149, "price": 1.10, "provider": "Google"},
    {"name": "DeepSeek V3.2", "intel": 42, "speed": 31, "price": 0.30, "provider": "DeepSeek"},
    {"name": "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "intel": 36, "speed": 193, "price": 0.40, "provider": "NVIDIA"},
    {"name": "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "intel": 33, "speed": 206, "price": 0.30, "provider": "OpenAI"},
]

MODELS_CHART = [m for m in MODELS if m["speed"] is not None]

PROVIDER_COLORS = {
    "Google": ACCENT_BLUE,
    "OpenAI": ACCENT_PURPLE,
    "Anthropic": ACCENT_RED,
    "NVIDIA": ACCENT_GREEN,
    "DeepSeek": ACCENT_TEAL,
    "xAI": ACCENT_ORANGE,
    "Zhipu": ACCENT_PINK,
    "Muse": TEXT_SECONDARY,
}

# =============================================================================
# CREATE CANVAS
# =============================================================================
img = Image.new("RGB", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# =============================================================================
# FONTS
# =============================================================================
f_title = load_font("display", 180)
f_subtitle = load_font("sans", 50)
f_meta = load_font("mono", 28)

f_big_num = load_font("display", 260)
f_big_label = load_font("sans_bold", 38)
f_big_context = load_font("sans", 32)

f_section_title = load_font("display", 90)
f_section_sub = load_font("sans", 34)

f_chart_label = load_font("sans_bold", 28)
f_chart_value = load_font("mono_bold", 32)
f_chart_axis = load_font("mono", 24)
f_model_name = load_font("sans", 26)
f_model_name_bold = load_font("sans_bold", 26)
f_small = load_font("sans", 24)
f_tiny = load_font("mono", 20)
f_rank = load_font("mono_bold", 24)

# =============================================================================
# MARGINS
# =============================================================================
MARGIN = 170
CONTENT_W = WIDTH - 2 * MARGIN

# =============================================================================
# HEADER
# =============================================================================
y_pos = MARGIN

# Top accent line
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 6], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
y_pos += 70

# Title
draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), "FRONTIER AI MODELS", font=f_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y_pos += 210

# Subtitle
draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), "Intelligence · Speed · Cost", font=f_subtitle, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
y_pos += 60
# Index note
draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), "Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0", font=f_meta, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
y_pos += 110

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# BIG STATS ROW
# =============================================================================
stats = [
    ("57", "Highest Intelligence", "Gemini 3.1 Pro & GPT-5.4", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("206", "Fastest Output", "gpt-oss-120B tokens/sec", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("33×", "Price Spread", "$0.30 → $10.00 per 1M tokens", ACCENT_TEAL),
]

stat_box_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (val, label, context, color) in enumerate(stats):
    x = MARGIN + i * stat_box_w
    # Top accent bar
    draw.rectangle([x, y_pos, x + stat_box_w - 50, y_pos + 5], fill=color)
    # Big number
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 40), val, font=f_big_num, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    # Label
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 320), label.upper(), font=f_big_label, fill=color)
    # Context
    draw.text((x, y_pos + 380), context, font=f_big_context, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y_pos += 520

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: INTELLIGENCE RANKING
# =============================================================================
def draw_intelligence_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "INTELLIGENCE RANKINGS", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0  —  10 benchmark average", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 100

    bar_h = 60
    bar_gap = 32
    max_score = 60
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 460

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS[:10]):
        score = m["intel"]
        bar_w = int((score / max_score) * bar_max_w)
        
        # Rank
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 14), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_rank, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        
        # Model name
        draw.text((MARGIN + 75, y + 14), m["name"], font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        # Bar background
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        # Bar fill
        if score >= 55:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        elif score >= 45:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        
        # Score
        draw.text((MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w + 40, y + 14), str(score), font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 60

y_pos = draw_intelligence_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: SPEED COMPARISON
# =============================================================================
def draw_speed_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "OUTPUT SPEED", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Tokens per second  —  the fastest model is not the smartest", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 100

    bar_h = 60
    bar_gap = 32
    max_speed = 220
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 460

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS_CHART):
        speed = m["speed"]
        bar_w = int((speed / max_speed) * bar_max_w)
        
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 14), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_rank, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 75, y + 14), m["name"], font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        if speed >= 180:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        elif speed >= 100:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w + 40, y + 14), str(speed), font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 60

y_pos = draw_speed_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: PRICING LANDSCAPE
# =============================================================================
def draw_pricing_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "PRICING LANDSCAPE", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "USD per 1 million tokens (blended input/output)", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 100

    bar_h = 60
    bar_gap = 32
    max_price = 12.0
    bar_max_w = CONTENT_W - 460

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS_CHART):
        price = m["price"]
        bar_w = int((price / max_price) * bar_max_w)
        
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 14), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_rank, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 75, y + 14), m["name"], font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        
        if price >= 8.0:
            bar_color = ACCENT_RED
        elif price >= 4.0:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        elif price >= 1.5:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER
        
        draw.rectangle([MARGIN + 460, y, MARGIN + 460 + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 460 + bar_max_w + 40, y + 14), f"${price:.2f}", font=f_chart_value, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 60

y_pos = draw_pricing_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: TRADE-OFF ANALYSIS (BUBBLE CHART)
# =============================================================================
def draw_tradeoff_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "THE TRADE-OFF", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Intelligence vs Speed vs Cost  —  bubble size = price", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 130

    chart_w = CONTENT_W
    chart_h = 1600
    chart_x = MARGIN
    chart_y = y

    # Background
    draw.rectangle([chart_x, chart_y, chart_x + chart_w, chart_y + chart_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Grid lines
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gx = chart_x + int(chart_w * i / 6)
        draw.line([(gx, chart_y), (gx, chart_y + chart_h)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gy = chart_y + int(chart_h * i / 6)
        draw.line([(chart_x, gy), (chart_x + chart_w, gy)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Axis labels
    draw.text((chart_x + chart_w // 2 - 140, chart_y + chart_h + 45), "INTELLIGENCE SCORE →", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    
    # Y-axis label drawn vertically
    label_y_text = "OUTPUT SPEED →"
    ly = chart_y + chart_h // 2 - 120
    for ch in label_y_text:
        draw.text((chart_x - 100, ly), ch, font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
        ly += 22

    # Plot bubbles
    min_intel, max_intel = 30, 60
    min_speed, max_speed = 20, 220

    for m in MODELS_CHART:
        ix = chart_x + int(((m["intel"] - min_intel) / (max_intel - min_intel)) * chart_w)
        iy = chart_y + chart_h - int(((m["speed"] - min_speed) / (max_speed - min_speed)) * chart_h)
        
        # Bubble radius based on price
        r = 24 + int(math.log(m["price"] + 0.5) * 30)
        
        color = PROVIDER_COLORS.get(m["provider"], TEXT_SECONDARY)
        
        # Glow effect - softer, more refined
        for g in range(5, 0, -1):
            glow_r = r + g * 10
            glow_color = blend_color(color, BG, 0.78 + g * 0.04)
            draw.ellipse([ix - glow_r, iy - glow_r, ix + glow_r, iy + glow_r], fill=glow_color)
        
        # Bubble
        draw.ellipse([ix - r, iy - r, ix + r, iy + r], fill=color, outline=TEXT_PRIMARY, width=2)
        
        # Label
        short_name = m["name"].replace(" (max)", "").replace(" (xhigh)", "").replace(" (high)", "")
        if "Gemini 3.1" in short_name:
            short_name = "G 3.1 Pro"
        elif "Gemini 3 Flash" in short_name:
            short_name = "G 3 Flash"
        elif "GPT-5.4" in short_name:
            short_name = "GPT-5.4"
        elif "Claude Opus" in short_name:
            short_name = "C Opus"
        elif "Claude Sonnet" in short_name:
            short_name = "C Sonnet"
        elif "gpt-oss" in short_name:
            short_name = "oss-120B"
        elif "NVIDIA" in short_name:
            short_name = "Nemotron"
        elif "DeepSeek" in short_name:
            short_name = "DeepSeek"
        elif "Grok" in short_name:
            short_name = "Grok"
        elif "GLM" in short_name:
            short_name = "GLM"
        elif "Muse" in short_name:
            short_name = "Muse"
        
        tw, th = get_text_size(draw, short_name, f_tiny)
        lx = ix - tw // 2
        ly = iy + r + 12
        if ly + th > chart_y + chart_h - 15:
            ly = iy - r - th - 12
        if lx < chart_x + 10:
            lx = chart_x + 10
        if lx + tw > chart_x + chart_w - 10:
            lx = chart_x + chart_w - 10 - tw
        
        # Small shadow for readability
        draw.text((lx+1, ly+1), short_name, font=f_tiny, fill=BG)
        draw.text((lx, ly), short_name, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Legend box
    legend_y = chart_y + 45
    legend_x = chart_x + chart_w - 380
    draw.rectangle([legend_x - 20, legend_y - 20, legend_x + 360, legend_y + 340], fill=BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    draw.text((legend_x, legend_y), "PROVIDER", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    legend_y += 50
    
    providers = [
        ("Google", ACCENT_BLUE), ("OpenAI", ACCENT_PURPLE), ("Anthropic", ACCENT_RED),
        ("NVIDIA", ACCENT_GREEN), ("DeepSeek", ACCENT_TEAL), ("xAI", ACCENT_ORANGE), ("Zhipu", ACCENT_PINK)
    ]
    for prov, col in providers:
        draw.ellipse([legend_x, legend_y, legend_x + 20, legend_y + 20], fill=col)
        draw.text((legend_x + 36, legend_y - 1), prov, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        legend_y += 38

    return chart_y + chart_h + 110

y_pos = draw_tradeoff_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: KEY INSIGHTS
# =============================================================================
def draw_insights_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "KEY INSIGHTS", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125

    insights = [
        ("BEST INTELLIGENCE", "Gemini 3.1 Pro & GPT-5.4 tied at 57", "Mid-to-high cost ($4.50–$5.60)", ACCENT_BLUE),
        ("BEST VALUE", "gpt-oss-120B — 206 tok/s, $0.30", "Lowest intelligence (33)", ACCENT_AMBER),
        ("BALANCED PICK", "Gemini 3 Flash — 46 intel, 149 tok/s, $1.10", "Strong middle ground", ACCENT_TEAL),
        ("PREMIUM TIER", "Claude Opus 4.6 — 53 intel, 40 tok/s, $10.00", "Slowest & most expensive", ACCENT_RED),
    ]

    card_w = (CONTENT_W - 60) // 2
    card_h = 280
    for i, (title, line1, line2, color) in enumerate(insights):
        row = i // 2
        col = i % 2
        cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + 60)
        cy = y + row * (card_h + 60)
        
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + card_w, cy + card_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 6, cy + card_h], fill=color)
        
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 50), title, font=f_big_label, fill=color)
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 120), line1, font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 185), line2, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    return y + 2 * (card_h + 60) + 70

y_pos = draw_insights_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, WIDTH - MARGIN, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: METHODOLOGY
# =============================================================================
def draw_methodology(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "ABOUT THE INDEX", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    
    text = "The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0 aggregates performance across 10 independent evaluations: GDPval-AA, τ²-Bench Telecom, Terminal-Bench Hard, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, and CritPt. Scores represent holistic capability across coding, agentic tasks, knowledge, and reasoning. All measurements conducted independently by Artificial Analysis using standardized conditions."
    
    words = text.split()
    line = ""
    line_h = 44
    for word in words:
        test = line + " " + word if line else word
        tw, _ = get_text_size(draw, test, f_small)
        if tw > CONTENT_W:
            draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
            y += line_h
            line = word
        else:
            line = test
    if line:
        draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
        y += line_h

    return y + 100

y_pos = draw_methodology(y_pos)

# =============================================================================
# FOOTER
# =============================================================================

# Font paths

FONTS = {
    "display": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Bold.ttf",
    "display_reg": FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Regular.ttf",
    "sans": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Regular.ttf",
    "sans_bold": FONT_DIR + "InstrumentSans-Bold.ttf",
    "mono": FONT_DIR + "JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf",

    "serif": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Regular.ttf",
    "serif_italic": FONT_DIR + "CrimsonPro-Italic.ttf",
}

def load_font(name, size):
    return ImageFont.truetype(FONTS[name], size)

def hex_to_rgb(hex_color):
    hex_color = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(hex_color[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

def rgb_to_hex(rgb):
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex((int(r1 + (r2 - r1) * t), int(g1 + (g2 - g1) * t), int(b1 + (b2 - b1) * t)))

def get_text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

]

    return tuple(int(hex_color[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % rgb

def draw_speed_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "OUTPUT SPEED", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Tokens per second  —  the fastest model is not the smartest", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 100

    bar_h = 60
    bar_gap = 32
    max_speed = 220
    bar_start = MARGIN + 480
    bar_max_w = MAX_X - bar_start

    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS_CHART):
        speed = m["speed"]
        bar_w = int((speed / max_speed) * bar_max_w)
        
        draw.text((MARGIN, y + 14), f"{i+1:02d}", font=f_rank, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)
        draw.text((MARGIN + 75, y + 14), m["name"], font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        
        draw.rectangle([bar_start, y, bar_start + bar_max_w, y + bar_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)

        elif speed >= 100:
            bar_color = ACCENT_TEAL
        else:
            bar_color = ACCENT_BLUE
        
        draw.rectangle([bar_start, y, bar_start + bar_w, y + bar_h], fill=bar_color)

        y += bar_h + bar_gap
    
    return y + 60

y_pos = draw_speed_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, MAX_X, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)

def draw_pricing_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "PRICING LANDSCAPE", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "USD per 1 million tokens (blended input/output)", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    bar_start = MARGIN + 480
    bar_max_w = MAX_X - bar_start

y_pos = draw_pricing_section(y_pos)

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, MAX_X, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: TRADE-OFF ANALYSIS (BUBBLE CHART)
# =============================================================================
def draw_tradeoff_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "THE TRADE-OFF", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Intelligence vs Speed vs Cost  —  bubble size = price", font=f_section_sub, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 130

    chart_x = MARGIN
    chart_w = MAX_X - chart_x + 1  # Inclusive width within margin
    chart_h = 1600
    chart_y = y

    # Background
    draw.rectangle([chart_x, chart_y, MAX_X, chart_y + chart_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Grid lines
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gx = chart_x + int(chart_w * i / 6)
        if gx <= MAX_X:
            draw.line([(gx, chart_y), (gx, chart_y + chart_h)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        gy = chart_y + int(chart_h * i / 6)
        draw.line([(chart_x, gy), (MAX_X, gy)], fill=GRID_LINE, width=1)

    # Axis labels
    tw, _ = get_text_size(draw, "INTELLIGENCE SCORE →", f_chart_axis)
    draw.text((chart_x + chart_w // 2 - tw // 2, chart_y + chart_h + 45), "INTELLIGENCE SCORE →", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    
    # Y-axis label drawn vertically
    label_y_text = "OUTPUT SPEED →"
    ly = chart_y + chart_h // 2 - 120
    for ch in label_y_text:
        draw.text((chart_x - 100, ly), ch, font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
        ly += 22

    # Plot bubbles
    min_intel, max_intel = 30, 60
    min_speed, max_speed = 20, 220

    for m in MODELS_CHART:
        ix = chart_x + int(((m["intel"] - min_intel) / (max_intel - min_intel)) * chart_w)
        iy = chart_y + chart_h - int(((m["speed"] - min_speed) / (max_speed - min_speed)) * chart_h)
        
        # Clamp to chart bounds with padding
        ix = max(chart_x + 70, min(ix, MAX_X - 70))
        iy = max(chart_y + 70, min(iy, chart_y + chart_h - 70))
        
        # Bubble radius based on price
        r = 24 + int(math.log(m["price"] + 0.5) * 30)
        
        color = PROVIDER_COLORS.get(m["provider"], TEXT_SECONDARY)
        
        # Glow effect
        for g in range(5, 0, -1):
            glow_r = r + g * 10
            glow_color = blend_color(color, BG, 0.78 + g * 0.04)
            draw.ellipse([ix - glow_r, iy - glow_r, ix + glow_r, iy + glow_r], fill=glow_color)
        
        # Bubble
        draw.ellipse([ix - r, iy - r, ix + r, iy + r], fill=color, outline=TEXT_PRIMARY, width=2)
        
        # Label
        short_name = m["name"].replace(" (max)", "").replace(" (xhigh)", "").replace(" (high)", "")
        if "Gemini 3.1" in short_name:
            short_name = "G 3.1 Pro"
        elif "Gemini 3 Flash" in short_name:
            short_name = "G 3 Flash"
        elif "GPT-5.4" in short_name:
            short_name = "GPT-5.4"
        elif "Claude Opus" in short_name:
            short_name = "C Opus"
        elif "Claude Sonnet" in short_name:
            short_name = "C Sonnet"
        elif "gpt-oss" in short_name:
            short_name = "oss-120B"
        elif "NVIDIA" in short_name:
            short_name = "Nemotron"
        elif "DeepSeek" in short_name:
            short_name = "DeepSeek"
        elif "Grok" in short_name:
            short_name = "Grok"
        elif "GLM" in short_name:
            short_name = "GLM"
        elif "Muse" in short_name:
            short_name = "Muse"
        
        tw, th = get_text_size(draw, short_name, f_tiny)
        lx = ix - tw // 2
        ly = iy + r + 12
        if ly + th > chart_y + chart_h - 15:
            ly = iy - r - th - 12
        if lx < chart_x + 10:
            lx = chart_x + 10
        if lx + tw > MAX_X - 10:
            lx = MAX_X - 10 - tw
        
        # Small shadow for readability
        draw.text((lx+1, ly+1), short_name, font=f_tiny, fill=BG)
        draw.text((lx, ly), short_name, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Legend box
    legend_w = 340
    legend_h = 340
    legend_y = chart_y + 45
    legend_x = MAX_X - legend_w - 30
    draw.rectangle([legend_x, legend_y, legend_x + legend_w, legend_y + legend_h], fill=BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
    draw.text((legend_x + 20, legend_y + 20), "PROVIDER", font=f_chart_axis, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    legend_y += 55
    
    providers = [
        ("Google", ACCENT_BLUE), ("OpenAI", ACCENT_PURPLE), ("Anthropic", ACCENT_RED),
        ("NVIDIA", ACCENT_GREEN), ("DeepSeek", ACCENT_TEAL), ("xAI", ACCENT_ORANGE), ("Zhipu", ACCENT_PINK)
    ]
    for prov, col in providers:
        draw.ellipse([legend_x + 20, legend_y, legend_x + 40, legend_y + 20], fill=col)
        draw.text((legend_x + 56, legend_y - 1), prov, font=f_tiny, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        legend_y += 38

    return chart_y + chart_h + 110

y_pos = draw_tradeoff_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, MAX_X, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: KEY INSIGHTS
# =============================================================================
def draw_insights_section(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "KEY INSIGHTS", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125

    insights = [
        ("BEST INTELLIGENCE", "Gemini 3.1 Pro & GPT-5.4 tied at 57", "Mid-to-high cost ($4.50–$5.60)", ACCENT_BLUE),
        ("BEST VALUE", "gpt-oss-120B — 206 tok/s, $0.30", "Lowest intelligence (33)", ACCENT_AMBER),
        ("BALANCED PICK", "Gemini 3 Flash — 46 intel, 149 tok/s, $1.10", "Strong middle ground", ACCENT_TEAL),
        ("PREMIUM TIER", "Claude Opus 4.6 — 53 intel, 40 tok/s, $10.00", "Slowest & most expensive", ACCENT_RED),
    ]

    card_w = (CONTENT_W - 60) // 2
    card_h = 280
    for i, (title, line1, line2, color) in enumerate(insights):
        row = i // 2
        col = i % 2
        cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + 60)
        cy = y + row * (card_h + 60)
        
        card_right = min(cx + card_w, MAX_X)
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, card_right, cy + card_h], fill=CARD_BG, outline=GRID_LINE, width=1)
        draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 6, cy + card_h], fill=color)
        
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 50), title, font=f_big_label, fill=color)
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 120), line1, font=f_model_name_bold, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
        draw.text((cx + 50, cy + 185), line2, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    return y + 2 * (card_h + 60) + 70

y_pos = draw_insights_section(y_pos)

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, MAX_X, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 100

# =============================================================================
# SECTION: METHODOLOGY
# =============================================================================
def draw_methodology(y):
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), "ABOUT THE INDEX", font=f_section_title, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    y += 125
    
    text = "The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0 aggregates performance across 10 independent evaluations: GDPval-AA, τ²-Bench Telecom, Terminal-Bench Hard, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, and CritPt. Scores represent holistic capability across coding, agentic tasks, knowledge, and reasoning. All measurements conducted independently by Artificial Analysis using standardized conditions."
    
    words = text.split()
    line = ""
    line_h = 44
    for word in words:
        test = line + " " + word if line else word
        tw, _ = get_text_size(draw, test, f_small)
        if tw > CONTENT_W:
            draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
            y += line_h
            line = word
        else:
            line = test
    if line:
        draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=f_small, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
        y += line_h

    return y + 100

y_pos = draw_methodology(y_pos)

# =============================================================================
# FOOTER
# =============================================================================
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y_pos, MAX_X, y_pos + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y_pos += 60

draw.text((MARGIN, y_pos), "Data: artificialanalysis.ai · Intelligence Index v4.0 · April 2026", font=f_meta, fill=TEXT_TERTIARY)

# =============================================================================
# SAVE
# =============================================================================
img.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", dpi=(DPI, DPI))
print("Poster saved to /app/output/final_poster.png")
print(f"Dimensions: {WIDTH}x{HEIGHT}")
